name: Khwaja 'Abdullah Ansari of Herat
credit: 'Abdullah Ansari with Abu Ahmad, Safavid Shiraz, second half of the 16th century · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Khwaja 'Abdullah Ansari (1006-1089), called the Pir of Herat, was a Hanbali theologian and Sufi master born at Kuhandiz near Herat, in what is now Afghanistan. He taught in Herat under the Ghaznavids and Seljuks, and wrote in both Arabic and Persian.

He is remembered above all for his Persian prayers, the Munajat-nama, written in rhymed prose with scattered quatrains, which set a model for later Persian devotional writing. His commentary and Sufi treatises, among them the Tabaqat al-Sufiyya and the Sad Maydan, were also widely read.
